instruction.text: Drag the buildings to the image to complete the Maya city-state.

feedback.finish: Building the first Maya cities began in around 750 BC, but it wasn’t until 500 BC that much of their grand architecture was finished.

instruction.text: Select the pyramid that matches the description.

atoms.a: The Pyramid of Kukulkan in Chichen Itza has 4 sides, each with 9 platforms and a staircase in the middle. The four staircases have a total of 365 steps, one for each day of the year.
The Pyramid of the Magician in Uxmal is the biggest monument in the city. It is the only known Maya temple with an oval structure.
atoms.sound: The Pyramid of the Magician in Oozmarl is the biggest monument in the city. It is the only known Maya temple with an oval structure.

atoms.a: The Temple of the Sun is one of three temples that makes up the Group of the Cross, all found in Palenque. This temple is dedicated to the god of war.

instruction.text: Find and select the ceremonial centre of the city.

feedback.finish: The richest and most important people in Maya society lived in the ceremonial centres, where the temples were located. The ordinary people lived on the outskirts of the cities.

hint.label: Plaza
hint.text: Plazas are large, open areas that are found in many cities.

atoms.b: Ancient Maya cities typically had several plazas. The main ((++plaza plozo)) was used for religious ceremonies because it was often next to the main temple.
There were also lots of smaller plazas where they would hold ((++markets marks)) and trade goods with citizens and other Maya cities.
Lots of Maya cities also had ball courts. The ((++courts caughts)) were used to play a popular Maya game called pitz.

feedback.finish: Sacbe is Mayan for “white road”. These paved roads were built to connect different city-states.

instruction.text: The longest known sacbe connected the cities of Yaxuna and Cobá. Draw a line along the path of the sacbe.
instruction.sound: The longest known sacbay connected the cities of Yaxuna and Cobá. Draw a line along the path of the sacbay.

finish.text: This sacbe runs 62 miles from Yaxuna to Cobá. Many of these roads can still be seen today and tell us about the connection between different cities in the past.
finish.sound: This sacbe runs 62 miles from Yaksuna to Cobá. Many of these roads can still be seen today and tell us about the connection between different cities in the past.

hint.text: More than one answer can be correct.

end.text: The main links between the city-states came about through trading goods, such as salt and special quetzal feathers. Warfare was also common as they fought over resources.
end.sound: The main links between the city-states came about through trading goods, such as salt and special kwettsal feathers. Warfare was also common as they fought over resources.
